answer: An agent economy can require each participant to lock a scarce token before bidding, with funds held through a long dispute horizon. A challenger who proves that supposedly independent agents share one operator can trigger a slash, sending part of their deposits to the challenger. This does not prove unique personhood, but forces an attacker to buy and immobilize capital for every fake identity, risk losing it, and forge evidence to evade detection. The reef is that honest agents also pay this cost.
